headline: End of an era: Lionel Messi retires from Argentina national team
summary: The football world pays homage to the superstar after 20 years of service, with teammates and fans calling him the 'greatest of all time'.
details: Argentine superstar Lionel Messi has decided to retire from the national team, bringing an end to a legendary 20-year international career.
Teammates and fans worldwide have expressed their grief and shock, describing the announcement as a heartbreaking moment for the sport.
Fellow player Angel Di Maria expressed his sadness, stating it is hard to read that Messi will no longer wear the sky blue and white jersey.
Many tributes have called him the 'greatest of all time' and an 'eternal' figure who redefined the beautiful game and inspired millions.
Messi's farewell message, spanning three pages, reflected on his journey and serves as a golden symbol of his time with the national squad.
The football community continues to celebrate his extraordinary achievements and the achievements he fulfilled all his dreams with Argentina.
caption:
20 years, one golden legacy. Lionel Messi says goodbye to the Argentina national team.

Argentine superstar Lionel Messi has decided to retire from the national team, bringing an end to a legendary 20-year international career.

Teammates and fans worldwide have expressed their grief and shock, describing the announcement as a heartbreaking moment for the sport.

Fellow player Angel Di Maria expressed his sadness, stating it is hard to read that Messi will no longer wear the sky blue and white jersey.

Many tributes have called him the 'greatest of all time' and an 'eternal' figure who redefined the beautiful game and inspired millions.

Messi's farewell message, spanning three pages, reflected on his journey and serves as a golden symbol of his time with the national squad.

The football community continues to celebrate his extraordinary achievements and the achievements he fulfilled all his dreams with Argentina.

headline_marked: 71-run win: [[Bangladesh crush Indonesia]] in Asia Cup opener
headline: 71-run win: Bangladesh crush Indonesia in Asia Cup opener
summary: Nahida Akter's 3-15 and a clinical bowling attack bowl out Indonesia for 58, securing a dominant start for the Tigresses.
details: Bangladesh began their Women’s Asia Cup T20 campaign with a dominant 71-run victory over Indonesia at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Monday.
Defending a total of 129, the Tigresses' bowling attack was clinical, bowling out Indonesia for just 58 runs in 17.3 overs.
Left-arm spinner Nahida Akter starred with the ball, claiming 3-15 in her four overs, while pacer Marufa Akter removed both Indonesian openers early on.
Earlier, Sobhana Mostary top-scored with 41 off 42 balls, and Dilara Akter contributed 27 off 31, helping Bangladesh reach 129-8 after being sent in to bat.
Shorna Akter provided a late surge of momentum, hitting an unbeaten 31 off just 18 balls to push the total close to 130.
Indonesia struggled throughout the innings, with only Maria Corazon managing to reach double figures with 12 runs.
Bangladesh will next face Sri Lanka on September 6 before concluding their group-stage matches against the UAE on September 8.
The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals on September 10 and 11, with the final scheduled for September 13.
caption:
A dominant start for the Tigresses! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh crush Indonesia by 71 runs to open their Asia Cup campaign.

Bangladesh began their Women’s Asia Cup T20 campaign with a dominant 71-run victory over Indonesia at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Monday.

Defending a total of 129, the Tigresses' bowling attack was clinical, bowling out Indonesia for just 58 runs in 17.3 overs.

Left-arm spinner Nahida Akter starred with the ball, claiming 3-15 in her four overs, while pacer Marufa Akter removed both Indonesian openers early on.

Earlier, Sobhana Mostary top-scored with 41 off 42 balls, and Dilara Akter contributed 27 off 31, helping Bangladesh reach 129-8 after being sent in to bat.

Shorna Akter provided a late surge of momentum, hitting an unbeaten 31 off just 18 balls to push the total close to 130.

Indonesia struggled throughout the innings, with only Maria Corazon managing to reach double figures with 12 runs.

Bangladesh will next face Sri Lanka on September 6 before concluding their group-stage matches against the UAE on September 8.

The top two teams from each group will advance to the semi-finals on September 10 and 11, with the final scheduled for September 13.
